governing_question: Can this signal earn and keep the right to influence capital allocation?

methodology.promotion_rule: No signal reaches production without a fixed executable rule, validated data, realistic costs, regime tests, a look-ahead review, a deactivation rule and out-of-sample evidence.

signals.name: U.S. legislative policy alpha
signals.hypothesis: The operative text and official procedural status of U.S. federal legislation may predict abnormal returns in liquid public-market exposures when the legislation creates a direct, specific, material and time-bounded economic effect that can be mapped before entry.
predictor_assets: contemporaneously available official fiscal and committee estimates
target_assets: liquid U.S. sector and industry ETFs
signals.horizon: 1, 5, 20 and 60 regular-session trading days after an executable event
applicable_regimes: final-chamber passage of economically operative legislation
direct fiscal, tax, trade, procurement, regulatory, sanctions or export-control change
invalid_regimes: target-specific earnings, merger or other material news overlapping entry
signals.mechanism: Binding legislation can change expected revenue, costs, taxes, capital access, competition, procurement demand or legal constraints before the market fully incorporates the detailed language.
signals.decay_mechanism: Legislation may be anticipated, implementation may be delayed, exposure mapping may be too diffuse, or market participants may parse the language faster once the workflow becomes common.
signals.canonical_rule: Begin with just-passed legislation only: after identical operative text has completed final congressional passage and the text is public, apply the frozen five-part tradeability gate, map qualifying beneficiaries and losers without using post-event prices, enter at the next regular-session open and use the fifth regular-session close as the primary exit.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate after at least 30 untouched eligible events if benchmark-adjusted after-cost expectancy is non-positive, or immediately if official event timestamps, operative text or pre-entry exposure mappings cannot be reproduced.
signals.benchmark: The matching sector or industry ETF, or an equal-weighted unaffected same-subindustry peer basket selected before entry
signals.data_source: Congress.gov API bill, action, text and House-vote records; authenticated legislative text from Congress.gov or GovInfo; timestamped market prices and spreads
signals.notes: The semiconductor idea was the first example, not the selection universe. Canonical version 1 studies just-passed legislation. The about-to-pass pre-passage variant is preserved but remains blocked until its probability and amendment-risk rules are frozen.

metadata.canonical_scope: final congressional passage with public operative text
metadata.enhanced_scope: scheduled or highly probable pre-passage events
tradeability_gate: final congressional passage in identical operative form
quantifiable materiality from contemporaneously available official information
implementation or binding effect within 24 months

signals.name: Public Apple call accuracy tracker
signals.hypothesis: The account's timestamped public Apple campaigns may contain directional or timing skill beyond chance and benchmark drift.
signals.mechanism: Potential discretionary insight into Apple positioning, valuation or market structure.
signals.decay_mechanism: Skill may be episodic, calls may become crowded, or public posting may lag actual execution.
signals.canonical_rule: Count one continuous thesis as one campaign; score all timestamped bullish and bearish campaigns using predeclared horizons and disclosed exits.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if the complete public ledger shows no positive abnormal expectancy after a minimum sample or if posts cease to be executable.
signals.benchmark: AAPL buy-and-hold plus SPY and QQQ
signals.data_source: Timestamped public posts, AAPL prices and reproducible option marks
signals.notes: Scaled entries are not independent forecasts. Options P&L requires premium data or a reproducible proxy.

signals.name: 90-period Hull moving-average regime filter
signals.hypothesis: A 90-period Hull moving average may improve trend participation or reduce adverse exposure in selected crypto markets and timeframes.
signals.mechanism: A smoother low-lag trend estimate may separate persistent direction from short-term noise.
signals.decay_mechanism: Crowding, timeframe overfitting and frequent reversals eliminate the edge after costs.
signals.canonical_rule: Test price-above/below and slope-change rules separately; never select the best-looking rule after viewing the test period.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate when rolling after-cost expectancy or trend-regime precision falls below the frozen acceptance threshold.
signals.benchmark: Buy-and-hold and a simple moving-average rule
signals.data_source: Reproducible OHLCV data at frozen bar sizes

signals.name: Bitcoin monthly VWAP reaction
signals.hypothesis: Bitcoin reacts predictably to monthly VWAP, potentially with stronger behavior near month-end.
signals.mechanism: Benchmark-aware positioning and inventory management may concentrate orders around monthly VWAP.
signals.decay_mechanism: The level becomes crowded or the visual relationship was selected retrospectively.
signals.canonical_rule: Predeclare touch, reclaim and exit definitions and compare month-end observations with all other sessions.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if touch/reclaim expectancy fails out of sample or disappears after realistic spread and slippage.
signals.data_source: Exchange trade data sufficient to reconstruct monthly VWAP without future bars

signals.name: Bitcoin as leveraged consumer-discretionary risk
signals.hypothesis: Consumer-discretionary risk appetite, represented by XLY or its constituents, may lead or explain Bitcoin returns in some liquidity regimes.
signals.mechanism: Both exposures may load on discretionary liquidity and long-duration risk appetite.
signals.decay_mechanism: The common factor changes or the measured relation is contemporaneous rather than predictive.
signals.canonical_rule: Test rolling beta and predeclared XLY-to-BTC lags against equity and liquidity controls.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if XLY adds no incremental predictive value beyond SPY, QQQ and liquidity controls.
signals.benchmark: SPY, QQQ, liquidity and broad risk-factor controls
signals.data_source: Adjusted XLY and BTC prices with synchronized decision timestamps

signals.name: Korea/Japan semiconductor lead into SanDisk
signals.hypothesis: Late Korean and Japanese semiconductor moves predicted SanDisk's following U.S. session during a temporary June-July 2026 regime.
signals.mechanism: Memory-chip information and participant flow may transmit from Asian trading hours into SNDK with a lag.
signals.decay_mechanism: Institutional accumulation, participant exit, better liquidity or discovery of the trade closes the lag.
signals.canonical_rule: Use only foreign-market information known before an executable SNDK entry; score the campaign before and after the claimed regime break.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate immediately when the post-break rolling relation or executable expectancy is no longer positive.
signals.benchmark: SNDK's own overnight information, SOXX and memory-equity controls
signals.data_source: Timestamped Asian-market and SNDK prices with executable session alignment
signals.notes: Historically interesting but currently blocked from capital because the claimed participant-created regime may have ended.

signals.name: Crypto leads U.S. equity rebound
signals.hypothesis: After a common macro risk dip, BTC, ETH, SOL and HYPE may progress through mechanically defined rebound stages before U.S. equity benchmarks and high-beta equity baskets.
signals.mechanism: Continuous crypto trading and faster risk re-entry may reveal improving liquidity appetite before U.S. equities fully recover.
signals.decay_mechanism: The relationship may be only a trading-hours artifact or equities may begin incorporating the same information immediately.
signals.canonical_rule: Using no more than 30 bars of recent realized volatility, compare the first timestamps at which each basket reaches local-low reversal, reference reclaim, trend confirmation and sustained recovery.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if lead time vanishes after market-hours adjustment or if crypto-specific shocks dominate the sample.
signals.benchmark: Equity-index futures and same-shock null ordering
signals.notes: Volatility-weighted aggregate is deferred; all four rebound definitions are canonical.

signals.name: BTC month-end deleveraging and new-month rebound
signals.hypothesis: BTC tends to weaken before the month boundary and rebound after the new month begins, potentially because risk is reduced into month-end and re-added afterward.
signals.mechanism: Calendar-linked deleveraging can create pre-boundary selling followed by risk re-entry and short-covering after the new month starts.
signals.decay_mechanism: The seasonal effect may be a short-sample artifact, become crowded, or be explained by quarter-end and weekday composition.
signals.canonical_rule: Freeze symmetric and long-only variants before testing: measure BTC returns over fixed windows before and after each month boundary, then test conditional leverage filters separately.
signals.deactivation_rule: Deactivate if the post-2026 held-out sample loses after-cost expectancy or if the effect is fully explained by quarter-end, weekday or trend controls.
signals.benchmark: All calendar windows, quarter-end controls and matched non-boundary windows
signals.data_source: Binance BTCUSDT perpetual and BTC spot data with UTC and U.S. close variants
signals.notes: Called S-009 during the initial bookmark conversation; the durable registry uses S-010 because S-009 already identifies the crypto-versus-equity rebound candidate.
